title.narrative: Assessing the risk and root causes of child labour in scrap metal recycling in Gujarat

description.narrative: Child labour remains a significant concern in Rajasthan's scrap metal recycling industry, where children are engaged in manual tasks including segregation, cleaning, packaging, and selling. Despite these risks, comprehensive data on child labour prevalence in scrap metal supply chains is severely lacking, making it difficult to identify root causes and develop targeted interventions. International companies, including Dutch firms like Krommenhoek Metals, operate with limited awareness of child labour risks within their regional supply chains, creating knowledge gaps that hinder effective remediation efforts.The project targets Krommenhoek Metals and its supply chain partner Gravita India Limited. Secondary beneficiaries include local scrap metal workers, communities in Rajasthan, and the broader international metal recycling industry seeking to implement responsible sourcing practices.Through systematic risk assessment and on-ground investigations, this project will identify child labour hotspots and socio-economic root causes within the scrap metal recycling supply chain. The initiative will establish a functioning social compliance system at Krommenhoek, develop evidence-based dialogue tools, and create sustainable procurement processes. Key deliverables include a comprehensive fair metal recycling supply chain training & best practices toolkit, implementation of improvement projects at Gravita's Phagi plant, and an international communication strategy to raise industry awareness. The project aims to bridge knowledge deficits, strengthen human rights due diligence in accordance with UN Guiding Principles, and create replicable models for responsible metal recycling that can be scaled across the industry globally.The project uses a multi-phase approach combining capacity building, assessment, and knowledge sharing activities. First, we establish a social compliance system at Krommenhoek through procurement team training, policy development, and supplier engagement tools. This includes workshops on socially compliant procurement and ongoing coaching support for implementation challenges.Second, we conduct baseline assessments at Gravita's Phagi plant to map current practices and identify improvement areas. This involves on-ground investigations to understand child labour hotspots and socio-economic root causes. We then develop and implement targeted improvement projects based on these findings, working with local partners to address specific risks.Third, we create knowledge products through stakeholder dialogue sessions, interviews, and collaborative analysis. These findings inform the development of a comprehensive Fair Metal Recycling Supply Chain Training & Best Practices Toolkit, which includes policies, instruments, training materials, and case studies.Finally, we implement a communication strategy that includes publications, press releases, photo documentation, and industry presentations. This approach ensures knowledge transfer through direct mailings, speaking engagements, and open-source resources that other companies can adopt. The methodology emphasises co-creation with partners and evidence-based dialogue to drive sustainable change in supply chain practices.'By opening up our site for this research, we’re taking a step towards more transparency and being able to share challenges and best practices. Not just for our company, but for the whole industry. This also adds to our wider goal of implementing best in class ESG framework at Gravita India Limited'- Rohit Nanoty, Gravita India Ltd.'As a family business, we believe our responsibility goes beyond trade. We want to make sure the metals we recycle or buy are not linked to human rights abuses. This project allows us to take practical steps to reduce risks and hopefully create positive impact.'- Bas Krommenhoek, Krommenhoek Metals
